headline: Six days without a run — the longest quiet stretch of the block, right on cue. Strength stayed live through the pause. Legs are banked; the crossing is now under two weeks out.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is coherent taper: running has gone dark for the better part of a week while strength has kept ticking over in short functional sessions, meaning the pause is selective rather than total. That distinction matters — the legs are getting genuine rest from impact load while the athlete stays physically engaged, which is exactly the shape you'd want heading into a multi-day self-supported effort. Steps have held near their strong baseline, so this isn't a body gone sedentary; daily movement is doing the job of keeping things ticking without adding fatigue. The one flashing indicator — the cardio load status reading as detraining — is a mechanical artifact of no logged running, not a fitness verdict, and should be read as such given how recently and how consistently the base was built. Recovery signals are mixed but not concerning in a taper context.
sections.trends: The medium-term shape is unambiguous: recent four-week volume sits well above the prior block, and year-to-date distance dwarfs the same point last year. That's a genuine step-change in running capacity built over months, and the current quiet week reads as a deliberate downshift off a high, not a stall. This is precisely the arc you want — sustained build, then a purposeful drawdown timed to an event — and it's consistent with the year-round hybrid readiness philosophy rather than a departure from it. Nothing in the trend suggests the base is eroding; a week of rest doesn't undo a block of that magnitude.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace remains strong from the last測 assessment, but there's no rolling baseline yet to track drift, so treat the single figure as a reference point rather than a live trend line. What matters right now is that the aerobic engine was demonstrably efficient in the final runs before the pause — controlled paces at moderate heart rates — and a short taper doesn't meaningfully blunt that. For the demands ahead, sustained low-intensity durability over days, threshold sharpness is not the limiting quality anyway.
sections.zones: The final week of running before the pause showed a sensible spread — several genuinely easy, Z1/Z2-dominant sessions bracketing one sharper effort that pushed into Z4 for a meaningful chunk. That last session was a real tempo stimulus, not a steady cruise dressed up by its average, and it's the right final hard touch before winding down. Since then, the only intensity has been low-level strength work sitting comfortably in the aerobic zones. For a taper, this distribution is appropriate: one quality hit banked, then quiet.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength sessions continue to sit low and aerobic, with the most recent ones logging no HR at all — worth noting only as a gap in the record, not a concern. Where strength HR is present, it tracks where you'd expect for functional work: mostly Z1 with modest Z2 spillover on the longer sessions. Nothing in the sensor-source pattern warrants attention this week.
sections.calendar: The rhythm here tells the real story: running frequency clustered densely through mid-July, then cut cleanly to zero, while strength kept a steadier cadence right up to a couple of days ago. That's a controlled handoff — impact work stops, low-load work persists — rather than a ragged drop-off. The consistency of the strength thread through the running pause is the detail worth holding onto; it means the athlete hasn't gone fully passive, just selectively unloaded.
sections.personal_bests: No PBs are in play during a taper, and none should be chased now. The standing bests — particularly the shorter-distance speed marks from last autumn — reflect a sharper, faster-focused window than the current ultra-oriented phase, so they're not the relevant yardstick for where training is pointed right now. Revisit them after the crossing, when the focus can swing back toward speed.

watch_items: Watch that the first run back after the crossing preparation lands easy and unremarkable, confirming the tempo and the long pause left the legs fresh rather than flat.
Watch whether strength stays live as light maintenance through to departure or goes quiet — either is defensible, but note which way it breaks.
Watch that steps and daily movement hold their baseline right up to travel, keeping the legs ticking rather than cold.
Watch how sleep tracks as logistics ramp — observe only, and don't let a rough night or two colour the read on readiness.
